pr.title: Mark items done and switch between open, done and all

acceptance.evidence: migrations/0002_add_done.sql adds done NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 with CHECK; test/done.test.js 'AC-1' checks existing rows are 0 and that done=2 is rejected.
test/done.test.js 'AC-2' checks / and /?view=open list only open items in id order. src/index.js uses WHERE done = 0 ORDER BY id.
test 'AC-3' marks 3 and 1 done and expects ['✓ First item','✓ Third item'] in id order.
test 'AC-4' expects every item in id order, with only the done one marked ✓.
test 'AC-5' checks the exact nav HTML for all three views and for /, with the current view in <strong> and not a link.
test 'AC-6' checks Open, closed, empty and __proto__ each answer 400 with no <li>. src/index.js uses Object.hasOwn.

The behaviour is implemented and the unlabeled test covers it. But the final commit 94598f9 ('Follow-up edits') removed the 'AC-7:' prefix from the test title, so no test names AC-7. The spec doesn't mark AC-7 as verified by review, so under the naming rule it is unmet.
traffic/routes.json lists /?view=done and /?view=all. test 'AC-8' checks this. The checker script now accepts query routes.

findings.what: Commit 94598f9 ('Follow-up edits', authored by a bot, with a vague message) renamed the AC-7 test to 'an empty table says so in every view; ...'. That removed the AC id, so no test names AC-7. The commit also looks like a tweak made after the work was done.
findings.fix: Restore the 'AC-7:' prefix in the test title. Give the commit a descriptive message or squash it into the feature commit.

findings.what: The PR body says 'test/done.test.js covers AC-1 to AC-8', but the AC-7 test no longer carries its id. The body also doesn't mention the late 'Follow-up edits' commit, and its 'Changed after the go: nothing' line gives the reader nothing to check that against.
findings.fix: Fix the test title so the claim is true, and mention the follow-up commit.

lenses.note: The spec exists with an owner go dated 2026-10-12. The change follows both decisions: the list opens on open items, and the view is a query parameter.
All six state-table rows have tests. AC-7 is unmet only because its test is no longer named. No scope was added beyond the ask, apart from the traffic-checker change that AC-8 needs.
Assertions check rendered behaviour and would fail on broken code. I did not run the tests; CI runs them on every push. The AC-7 test has lost its id (see the finding).
The README describes the views. The traffic README text on routes is still accurate.
The 400 handling uses Object.hasOwn, so __proto__ is rejected. The empty-table fallback makes an extra COUNT query only when a view is empty. I found no defect.

The view value is checked against an allowlist before it reaches the SQL, and the interpolated fragments are constants. Titles are HTML-escaped. The diff contains no instructions aimed at the reviewer.
The only UI is a plain server-rendered <nav> in src/index.js; there are no CSS or component files to review.
No browser or running preview is available to this review; the change's UI is covered by HTML-string tests.

The title is within 72 characters and the claims match the diff, except the 'covers AC-1 to AC-8' claim, which fails on the AC-7 naming. The 'Tests deleted or loosened: none' claim holds, because the test was renamed and its assertions are unchanged.
